# cache

Everything in Redis. Top-level because the worker and the kie.ai client need it too.

- `redis.py` — `get_redis()`: **the only Redis connection in the repo**. `get_text`/`set_text`/`delete_text` are for optimisation caches only: they swallow `RedisError` as a miss. Anything that must not lose a write uses `get_redis()` and picks its own failure policy.
- `queue.py` — `JobQueue(name=QueueName.X)`: a FIFO line on RQ. Which queues exist, their worker counts and priority: `config/settings.py` (`QueueName`, `InfraSettings.queues`). Tests (`OFM_RQ_ASYNC=false`) run it inline. `clone-links` has its own pool so a 120-link Generate never holds the default queue. `events` is top priority: events to the senders, integrations/senders/CLAUDE.md. `put(..., retry=Retry(...))` passes RQ retries through (the worker pool runs RQ's scheduler). `active_job_ids()` (recovery's view of live jobs; None = unknown) reads, in the order a job moves, each job queue's list, then its `:intermediate` list (rq BLMOVEs a dequeued job there; rq 3.0's worker registers the job's execution before the horse takes it off that list), then every worker's current execution (`get_current_job_id`) -- read in another order, a job just being dequeued was missed and failed as cut off (review #57).
- One container for the network queues: compose `worker` runs `python -m ofmhelpers.worker default clone-links events` -- `worker.QueueGroup`, a pool per queue (own processes and nice, so none waits behind another) forked from one parent that imported the app once (a container per queue held ~210 MB idle). A stop signal is passed to every pool; a pool that dies takes the container down (exit 1) so Docker restarts it whole. media / edit / previews keep their own service for their CPU and memory limits. Both deploys `up -d --remove-orphans`, so a service taken out of the compose file never runs on with old code.
